- Sharp post-IPO deleveraging: debt to equity moved 1.09 (FY23), 0.70 (FY24), 0.88 (FY25) to 0.13 (FY26), with non-current borrowings falling from Rs 101.8 Cr to Rs 55.9 Cr and current borrowings from Rs 116.8 Cr to Rs 24.4 Cr, while shareholders' funds rose from Rs 248.8 Cr to Rs 613.5 Cr (standalone FY26).

- Returns were diluted by the equity issue - the deck states ROCE and ROE 'declined majorly due to issue of equity shares during IPO', with ROCE at 17.4%, 22.3%, 17.0% and 10.3% and ROE at 19.7%, 24.9%, 21.0% and 8.3% across FY23-FY26.

- Strategically located and integrated manufacturing facilities enabling high-volume, low-cost, high-quality production, with proximity to petrochemical complexes, ICD Tumb and the Hazira (~150 km) and Nhava Sheva (~200 km) ports

bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Customer concentration without long-term contracts — The Risk Management section flags dependence on a limited number of major customers without long-term contracts as increasing revenue concentration risk. Credit exposure is concentrated among large, long-established international retail customers. Mitigation is diversification across new geographies, scaling the domestic branded business and entering adjacent product categories.
- Export dependence and geographic concentration — Exports constitute the predominant share of revenue, with Europe at approximately 58% of revenue, the United Kingdom at 12% and the United States at 12%, leaving only 17% domestic. A significant portion of the business is therefore exposed to a small number of developed-market geographies and to their tariff and trade-policy regimes.
- Raw material price volatility and supply chain disruption — From March 2026 the West Asia geopolitical situation caused a sharp increase in polymer prices together with significant global supply chain disruption, including congestion at Nhava Sheva and Mundra ports, extended transit timelines and constrained availability of certain critical grades. A portion of Q4 shipments was deferred into the subsequent period and the disruption continued into Q1 FY 2026-27. Mitigated by progressive price revisions, with the domestic business repriced in full and the export book following the contractual rollover mechanism.
- Intense competition in a fragmented market — The Company operates within a highly fragmented market with intense competition from established branded players and unorganised manufacturers. Competitive pricing pressure, particularly from unbranded products sold through traditional and e-commerce channels, may impact margins and market share growth. Mitigated by competing on design capability, scale, cost efficiency and compliance rather than price alone, with high switching costs from long product lifecycles, mould ownership and embedded supply chain integration.
- Currency risk on export receivables — Exchange rate fluctuations impacting foreign currency liabilities and export receivables may affect profitability and cash flows. Foreign currency export receivables are monitored against foreign currency payables and borrowings, which provides a partial natural hedge; residual exposure is reviewed periodically by management.
- Operating leverage / margin risk from unramped new capacity — Fixed costs associated with newly commissioned capacity at Khatalwada and the bamboo pilot facility at Guwahati were absorbed in full during the year while the corresponding volumes are yet to be fully realised. Employee benefit and contract labour costs also increased ahead of scale, and capacity utilisation fell to 67.4% from 79.5%, compressing operating margin.
- Liquidity risk — Inability to meet short-term obligations such as borrowings, payables and lease liabilities may result in payment delays, increased financing costs and operational disruptions affecting business continuity. Mitigated by monitoring rolling cash flow forecasts against available cash, bank balances, current investments and undrawn banking limits; the debt-to-equity ratio stood at 0.13 as at March 31, 2026 against 0.88 in the previous year following deployment of IPO net proceeds towards prepayment and repayment of borrowings.
- Interest rate risk — Fluctuations in interest rates may increase borrowing costs and create volatility in finance expenses and earnings. Exposure was substantially lowered as total borrowings reduced to INR 80.3 crore as at March 31, 2026 from INR 218.5 crore as at March 31, 2025; the mix of fixed and floating rate borrowings and facility pricing are reviewed periodically with lenders.

outlook.body: FY 2025-26 was a year of transition marked by substantial investment in manufacturing capacity and organisational capability. Installed capacity increased to 39,000 MT as at March 31, 2026 following commissioning of the expansion at the Khatalwada facility, with capacity utilisation for the year at 67.4% against 79.5% in FY 2024-25 (each computed with reference to installed capacity as at the respective year ends); the reduction reflects the expanded Khatalwada capacity being available for a full reporting period ahead of the corresponding volume ramp-up. Total polymer processed was 26,300 MT against 26,230 MT in FY 2024-25, of which recycled polymer volume rose to 8,022 MT from 7,136 MT. The Company operates 170 injection moulding machines across three plastic facilities: Daman (9,500 TPA, 62.9% utilisation, multi-component assembled and short-run parts, domestic and export), Silvassa (19,500 TPA, 85.3% utilisation, 100% EOU, high-volume single-shot parts, with a fully automated ASRS warehouse integrated with ERP and WMS), and Khatalwada, Gujarat (10,000 TPA, 56% utilisation on a pro-rata basis, 100% EOU, commissioned 2024, all types of injection-moulded consumerware). Once fully operational, the Khatalwada expansion is anticipated to double manufacturing capacity, creating headroom to meet customer demand over the next three years. During the year the Company operationalised its Tool Room at Khatalwada for in-house mould design and manufacture, introduced digital process controls at Khatalwada, and established in-house production of silicone gaskets and components. Subsequent to the balance sheet date, additional capacity of 2,000 MT that was under installation at year end has been commissioned, taking installed capacity to approximately 41,000 MT; orders have been placed for 14 additional injection moulding machines expected to add approximately 1,500 MT of capacity and come on stream during the fourth quarter of FY 2026-27; the balance capacity under the approved expansion programme is proposed to be ordered in a phased manner, aligned to product mix requirements and the equipment configuration required by specific customer programmes. On the bamboo initiative, the Company commissioned a bamboo pilot facility at Guwahati during the year and incorporated All Time Bamboo Private Limited as a wholly owned subsidiary; it has taken on lease a purpose-built 75,000 square feet facility at Madanpur, Guwahati with effect from May 2026 to serve as a dedicated bamboo board manufacturing unit with installed capacity of 3,000 cubic metres per annum in the first phase. Machinery for that facility has been ordered in full, with upstream board production at Guwahati and downstream processing and finishing of finished bamboo articles at Khatalwada; commercial contribution from the bamboo vertical is anticipated to commence from the fourth quarter of FY 2026-27. On renewable energy, 630 KWp of solar power capacity was installed at Khatalwada during the year, an additional 370 KWp solar installation is planned at Khatalwada, and 2 MWp of solar capacity is installed across the Company's manufacturing facilities.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: All Time Plastics is a 1971-established injection-moulded plastic consumerware manufacturer and India's largest exporter of plastic houseware (other than thermoware and insulated ware) and plastic furniture as recognised by PLEXCONCIL, exporting to 30 countries.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: The Company designs, manufactures and markets injection-moulded plastic houseware and lifestyle products across kitchen, storage, cleaning, bath, organisation and junior categories. It operates primarily as a B2B white-label manufacturing partner for international and Indian retailers and brands, complemented by a B2C business under its proprietary 'All Time' brand in India. It has entered the engineered bamboo consumerware ecosystem through a dedicated manufacturing platform in Guwahati, with a split-processing model where boards are made in Guwahati and value-added finishing is done at Khatalwada.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Global plastic houseware demand is steady and non-discretionary, driven by recurring household usage and replacement cycles.
- Structural shifts including increasing private-label penetration and supplier consolidation have reduced market fragmentation and strengthened the importance of scale and integrated design-to-delivery capabilities, so growth is primarily captured by manufacturers operating as strategic supply partners rather than commodity-based vendors.
- Global retailers are actively diversifying sourcing footprints to improve supply chain resilience, regulatory compliance and cost efficiency; the China Plus One strategy and proposed EU-India and US-India FTAs are expected to improve India's export competitiveness.
- The global consumerware market is projected to reach approximately USD 163 billion by 2029, registering a CAGR of 6.3%.
- The Indian consumerware market is projected to grow at a CAGR of 10.7% reaching approximately INR 498.7 billion by FY 2029-30; the Indian plastic houseware market is projected to reach INR 179 billion by FY 2029-30 at a CAGR of 12%, with the branded play projected to account for nearly 66% of the market at INR 117.4 billion by FY 2029-30, growing at a 13.0% CAGR between FY 2025-30.
- Margin lever: fixed costs of newly commissioned Khatalwada capacity and the Guwahati bamboo pilot were absorbed in full ahead of the corresponding volume ramp-up; as utilisation of the new facilities increases these investments are expected to contribute more meaningfully to earnings and returns.
- Mix lever: rising domestic share and growth of the branded 'All Time' business, which the Company treats as margin-accretive.
- Headwind flagged: from March 2026 the West Asia geopolitical situation caused a sharp increase in polymer prices and significant supply chain disruption including congestion at Nhava Sheva and Mundra ports, extended transit timelines and constrained availability of certain critical grades, deferring a portion of Q4 shipments into the subsequent period.
- Mitigant: price revisions have been progressively implemented across the customer base, with the domestic business repriced in full and the balance of the export book following the contractual rollover mechanism.
- Demand conditions and customer forecasts have remained firm throughout this period and the Company has not experienced order cancellations.
- The Company did not experience order cancellations during the Q4 FY2025-26 supply chain disruption, and customer forecasts remained unchanged.
- Demand conditions and customer forecasts have remained firm into the first quarter of FY 2026-27, with no order cancellations experienced.
- As at March 31, 2026, nineteen of the top twenty customer relationships were of more than five years' standing, of which seven exceeded fifteen years, supporting repeat orders and long customer tenures.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: FY 2025-26 was a year of transition marked by substantial investment in manufacturing capacity and organisational capability. Installed capacity increased to 39,000 MT as at March 31, 2026 following commissioning of the expansion at the Khatalwada facility, with capacity utilisation for the year at 67.4% against 79.5% in FY 2024-25 (each computed with reference to installed capacity as at the respective year ends); the reduction reflects the expanded Khatalwada capacity being available for a full reporting period ahead of the corresponding volume ramp-up. Total polymer processed was 26,300 MT against 26,230 MT in FY 2024-25, of which recycled polymer volume rose to 8,022 MT from 7,136 MT. The Company operates 170 injection moulding machines across three plastic facilities: Daman (9,500 TPA, 62.9% utilisation, multi-component assembled and short-run parts, domestic and export), Silvassa (19,500 TPA, 85.3% utilisation, 100% EOU, high-volume single-shot parts, with a fully automated ASRS warehouse integrated with ERP and WMS), and Khatalwada, Gujarat (10,000 TPA, 56% utilisation on a pro-rata basis, 100% EOU, commissioned 2024, all types of injection-moulded consumerware). Once fully operational, the Khatalwada expansion is anticipated to double manufacturing capacity, creating headroom to meet customer demand over the next three years. During the year the Company operationalised its Tool Room at Khatalwada for in-house mould design and manufacture, introduced digital process controls at Khatalwada, and established in-house production of silicone gaskets and components. Subsequent to the balance sheet date, additional capacity of 2,000 MT that was under installation at year end has been commissioned, taking installed capacity to approximately 41,000 MT; orders have been placed for 14 additional injection moulding machines expected to add approximately 1,500 MT of capacity and come on stream during the fourth quarter of FY 2026-27; the balance capacity under the approved expansion programme is proposed to be ordered in a phased manner, aligned to product mix requirements and the equipment configuration required by specific customer programmes. On the bamboo initiative, the Company commissioned a bamboo pilot facility at Guwahati during the year and incorporated All Time Bamboo Private Limited as a wholly owned subsidiary; it has taken on lease a purpose-built 75,000 square feet facility at Madanpur, Guwahati with effect from May 2026 to serve as a dedicated bamboo board manufacturing unit with installed capacity of 3,000 cubic metres per annum in the first phase. Machinery for that facility has been ordered in full, with upstream board production at Guwahati and downstream processing and finishing of finished bamboo articles at Khatalwada; commercial contribution from the bamboo vertical is anticipated to commence from the fourth quarter of FY 2026-27. On renewable energy, 630 KWp of solar power capacity was installed at Khatalwada during the year, an additional 370 KWp solar installation is planned at Khatalwada, and 2 MWp of solar capacity is installed across the Company's manufacturing facilities.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- In-house product and mould design and manufacturing team of 16 employees as at March 31, 2026, enabling design-to-delivery integration, shorter product development cycles and a regular cadence of new launches aligned to retailer refresh calendars
- Sticky customer relationships: as at March 31, 2026, nineteen of the top twenty customer relationships were of more than five years' standing, of which seven exceeded fifteen years
- High switching costs from long product lifecycles, mould ownership and embedded supply chain integration
- Strategically located and integrated manufacturing facilities enabling high-volume, low-cost, high-quality production, with proximity to petrochemical complexes, ICD Tumb and the Hazira (~150 km) and Nhava Sheva (~200 km) ports
- Scale: 170 injection moulding machines with 39,000 tonnes annual installed capacity; 76% of injection moulding machines were all-electric as at March 31, 2026, delivering lower power consumption, higher uptime and faster cycle times
- In-house Tool Room operationalised at Khatalwada, reducing dependence on external tooling and shortening development timelines
- In-house production of silicone gaskets and components, giving tighter quality control and greater product development flexibility
- Recognised by PLEXCONCIL with first place in Houseware Exports (other than thermoware and insulated ware) and first place in Plastic Furniture Exports for each of FY 2023-24 and FY 2024-25; received an award from Target for operational excellence, precision and agility
- Sustainability credentials as a supplier qualification: 100% energy-neutral manufacturing facilities since 2022, more than 25% of products made using recycled plastics, and third-party compliance approvals from Higg, EcoVadis and Amfori
- Experienced promoters with deep expertise in plastic consumerware manufacturing

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Input-cost and logistics shock] The West Asia crisis triggered an unprecedented spike in polymer prices from March 2026, while port congestion and container non-availability disrupted both raw material inflows and export shipments; management says raw material prices remain volatile and could see further near-term fluctuation depending on how the geopolitical situation evolves.
- [Trade policy] The EU-India FTA, the evolving US-India trade framework and the China+1 strategy are cited as expected tailwinds for India's sourcing attractiveness; management states the US business 'continues to gain momentum irrespective of tariff considerations', with growing project wins from marquee accounts.
- [Government MoU] ATPL entered an MoU with NECBDC, a statutory body under MDoNER, Government of India, and is empanelled as a Product and Market Development Partner for engineered bamboo initiatives, initially anchored in Assam and Nagaland, covering prototyping of bamboo boards and panels, process and quality standardisation, certification readiness including FSC, and domestic and export market linkage; the framework is explicitly non-exclusive and non-binding, with future commercial engagement to be pursued through separate agreements.
- [Incorporation date contradiction] The Company Snapshot states 'Incorporated in 1971', while the evolution timeline dates the 'Incorporation of our Company' to 2001 and attributes 1971 to setting up the small 'Chhaya Plastics' factory in Mumbai; the CIN shown is L25209MH2001PLC131139.
- [Corporate structure] Wholly owned subsidiaries are All Time Plastics Pte. Ltd. (incorporated 2024) and All Time Bamboo Private Limited (incorporated 2025, for bamboo consumerware); the company was listed on BSE and NSE in 2025 and crossed INR 500 crore in revenue in 2024.
